issues.legal_issue: A tenant who entered possession under a landlord cannot deny that landlord’s title while the tenancy continues when the tenant has previously acknowledged the title and provides no credible explanation for that acknowledgment.
material_facts: The tenant was the landlord’s employee and the parties executed a document agreeing to a lease of the premises, although execution was disputed; the tenant’s signatures appeared on every page.

In sworn testimony in earlier judicial proceedings, the tenant described the chain of title leading to the landlord and stated that the person from whom the tenant later claimed to have purchased the property had no title or interest in it.
The tenant offered no explanation for the earlier testimony or for the signatures on the lease document, and remained in possession while seeking to deny the landlord-tenant relationship.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was estopped from denying the landlord’s title while the tenancy continued, and the denial did not raise a triable issue.
issues.legal_principle: Section 116 of the Evidence Act estops a tenant from disputing the landlord’s title at the beginning of the tenancy, and the estoppel continues while the tenancy continues and the tenant has not surrendered possession. As explained in Vashu Deo v. Balkishan, [2002] 2 SCC 50, the rule may be adapted to the circumstances of an individual case and ceases to apply after eviction or where a paramount title extinguishes the landlord’s title. The tenant’s sworn admission and unexplained lease signatures supported applying the estoppel here.

rule.if: tenant_entered_possession_under_claimed_landlord and tenancy_continues and tenant_denies_landlord_title and tenant_previously_acknowledged_landlord_title_in_judicial_testimony and tenant_gives_no_credible_explanation

predicates.tenant_entered_possession_under_claimed_: The tenant entered possession of the premises under an arrangement with the person claiming to be the landlord.
predicates.tenancy_continues: The tenant remains in possession and has not surrendered possession to the landlord.
predicates.tenant_denies_landlord_title: The tenant denies that the person who inducted the tenant had title to the premises.
predicates.tenant_previously_acknowledged_landlord_: The tenant previously gave sworn testimony in judicial proceedings acknowledging the claimed landlord’s title to the premises.
predicates.tenant_gives_no_credible_explanation: The tenant gives no credible explanation for the prior acknowledgment or other evidence supporting the claimed tenancy arrangement.

issues.definition: When a tenant remains in possession after entering under a claimed landlord, a prior judicial acknowledgment of that landlord’s title without a credible explanation prevents the tenant from disputing that title during the continuing tenancy.

issues.legal_issue: Leave to defend in a summary eviction proceeding is warranted only when the tenant discloses facts that could disentitle the landlord from eviction and present a genuine issue for trial.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction on grounds including personal requirement and rent default.
The tenant sought leave to defend, denying the landlord-tenant relationship and claiming that the property had been purchased from another person.

The tenant’s denial was inconsistent with the tenant’s sworn acknowledgment of the landlord’s title and was unsupported by a credible explanation; the trial court found the defence false, frivolous, and unsustainable.
issues.conclusion: The tenant’s defence did not disclose a triable issue, so the trial court was justified in refusing leave to defend.
issues.legal_principle: Sub-sections (4) and (5) of Section 14 of the Bihar Buildings (Lease Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1982 require the tenant seeking leave to disclose facts that would disentitle the landlord from obtaining eviction. A court may assess whether an issue raised in the pleadings is genuinely triable; a defence that is sham, illusory, or practically moonshine does not suffice. The Court applied Charan Daas Duggal v. Brahma Nand, [1983] 1 SCC 30, and the Patna High Court decisions in Md. Fahimuddin v. Godhan Pd. Singh, (1992) 2 PLJR 352, and Bijoy Kumar Singh v. The State of Bihar & Ors., (1992) 1 PLJR 123, while holding that those authorities did not prevent the court from assessing whether a real triable issue arose.

predicates.summary_eviction_leave_application: The matter is an application for leave to defend in a summary eviction proceeding.
predicates.tenant_seeks_leave_to_defend: The tenant asks for permission to contest the eviction claim.
predicates.tenant_relies_on_defence_barred_by_tenan: The tenant relies on a denial of the landlord’s title despite facts that estop the tenant from making that denial.
predicates.tenant_discloses_no_other_genuine_fact_t: The tenant discloses no other genuine fact which, if established, could disentitle the landlord from eviction.

issues.definition: In a summary eviction proceeding, leave is refused when the tenant seeks to defend on an estopped denial and discloses no other genuine fact capable of defeating eviction.

issues.legal_issue: A revisional court should not set aside a reasoned refusal of leave to defend when the tenant has raised no triable issue.
material_facts: The trial court considered the parties’ pleadings, affidavits, and supporting documents and refused leave after finding the tenant’s defences false, frivolous, and legally unsustainable.
The High Court allowed the tenant’s revision on the view that the pleadings raised a triable issue.
The Supreme Court concluded that the tenant’s title denial was barred by estoppel and that no triable issue had been raised.
issues.conclusion: The High Court ought not to have interfered with the trial court’s reasoned order; the Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s order and restored the trial court’s order.
issues.legal_principle: In the exercise of revisional jurisdiction, interference was unwarranted with the trial court’s well-considered and reasoned refusal of leave where the tenant’s defence did not raise a triable issue under Section 14 of the Bihar Buildings (Lease Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1982.

predicates.revision_from_refusal_of_leave_to_defend: The proceeding is a revision challenging a trial court’s refusal to grant leave to defend an eviction claim.
predicates.trial_court_gave_reasoned_assessment: The trial court considered the pleadings, affidavits, and supporting material and explained its decision.
predicates.tenant_raised_no_triable_issue: The tenant’s disclosed facts do not present a genuine issue capable of affecting the landlord’s entitlement to eviction.

issues.definition: On revision from a reasoned refusal of leave, the refusal is restored when the tenant has raised no genuine triable issue.
